summary.headline: Kaynes Q1 FY27 revenue rose 40% to INR946 crore and EBITDA rose 31% to INR147.6 crore, but operating cash flow was negative INR259 crore as inventory and metering receivables rose.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 40% YoY to INR946 crore, driven by EMS (standalone EMS up 53%, overseas up 327% on the August Electronics acquisition), while smart metering fell 12% YoY to about INR204 crore as management deliberately curbed supplies over collections. EBITDA was INR147.6 crore at a 15.6% margin, with management flagging margin pressure from component and PCB cost inflation and lead times of 6 to 8 months. Negative operating cash flow was about INR259 crore (management also cited INR235 crore in another bridge), with inventory up about INR177 crore and receivables up about INR68 crore. OSAT and PCB commissioning remains guided for Q3 FY27, with a FY27 revenue target of INR450 to 500 crore across both.

segments.name: EMS (overall, incl. overseas)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR854 crore including GST, with 40% overall EMS growth and about 48% growth cited by management; collections of INR847 crore. Receivables in EMS were about INR613 crore at quarter end versus INR606 crore at the start.

segments.name: Smart metering (GridCrest)
segments.commentary: Sales about INR240 crore including GST against collections of INR88 crore, so production and supply were halted. Metering receivables rose from INR1,158 crore to INR1,311 crore; about INR200 crore was received in early July.

segments.name: OSAT (Kaynes Semicon)
segments.commentary: Capex to date about INR700 crore; government subsidy of INR170 crore received till July 2026. Commercial billing expected from Q3 FY27; Unit 2 on track for operation by Q3 FY27. Mitsui partnership for Japan access announced.

segments.name: PCB (Kaynes Circuit)
segments.commentary: Capex to date about INR500 crore, with about INR250 crore in transit. Commercial production to start next quarter; one global customer has requested the entire capacity and trials are ongoing with a vendor code approved.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth committed at 2x the market growth; no absolute top-line number given. Market grew about 17% in Q1.
OSAT and PCB combined FY27 revenue target INR450 to 500 crore, with revenue starting from Q3 FY27.
FY27 capex plan: about INR300 crore OSAT, about INR300 crore PCB and about INR250 crore EMS; Q1 spend about INR230 crore in total across these.
Management expects profitability to take a couple of quarters to normalise; FY27 described as a difficult, tough year.
Management expects receivables turnaround in the metering business and cash-positive position by end of FY27.
Working capital to be reported on a rolling 12-month basis going forward.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR180 crore (per management in the call), against a broader plan of about INR300 crore each for OSAT and PCB and about INR250 crore for EMS.
Capex in FY26 was INR473 crore for OSAT and INR324 crore for PCB.
Kaynes Semicon Unit 2 and Kaynes Circuit Chennai remain on track to be operational by Q3 FY27, despite minor slippage from West Asia-related equipment and logistics disruption.
Government subsidy of INR170 crore received in OSAT till July 2026, with more subsidies expected to fund further capex.

First 3U satellite in prototype; launch targeted mid-next year pending regulatory testing and an ISRO launch date (PSLV or GSLV). Titanium gas bottle manufacturing via Crio Precision and Aerotech for ISRO and DRDO.
demand_pricing: Order book of more than INR8,900 crore; management said Q1 order additions exceeded deliveries.

New logos include a second-largest Indian two-wheeler EV maker (serial supply begun after about 8 months of development), German and French global brands, and a leading Indian wireless operator; management cited about 72 customer visits in the quarter.
Component prices up about 30% to 35% per management; PCB prices up about 3x; lead times more than 6 to 8 months in some categories; PCB suppliers demanding advance payment.
FX impact on imports about 3.3% of import level, per management.
Pass-through to customers is on a quarter-on-quarter basis and may lag; management said agreements with strategic customers allow some price pass-through.
Aerospace recovered in the quarter; management said growth was seen across railways, automotive, aerospace and defence.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EMS growth excluding metering, and what is the EBITDA bridge and metering strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said overall EMS grew 40% and metering 28% (per one answer), with standalone EMS up 53% and metering down 12%. Lower other income after QIP proceeds (about 2.5 points on PBT/PAT) and higher depreciation were cited for margin pressure. Management said it is exploring models to divest the service portion of metering to keep receivables off the balance sheet, with details promised by February.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cash flow from operations and metering revenue for the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said operating cash flow was negative about INR259 crore (inventory up INR177 crore and receivables up INR68 crore), versus negative INR379 crore in Q1 FY26. Another bridge given later cited INR235 crore; the company's cash profit was about INR158 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the receivables, inventory and payables figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Total receivables (current and non-current) rose from about INR1,765 crore to INR1,925 crore. Inventory days were about 105 at Q1 end versus 96 earlier. Management said the 12-month rolling receivable days were about 163 and the quarterly figure about 190.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 revenue growth and the OSAT/PCB FY27 and FY28 scale-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management committed to 2x market growth without an absolute number, citing market volatility. OSAT and PCB together are targeted at INR450 to 500 crore of FY27 revenue from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How much of component cost inflation is captured and will gross margins compress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FX impact was about 3.3% of imports and back-to-back customer pass-through covers most of the rest, but pass-through may lag by a quarter. Ramesh Kunhikannan said FY27 would be a tough year with margins under pressure, though planned requirements would be met.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and PCB margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex plan is about INR300 crore each for OSAT and PCB and INR250 crore for EMS, with about INR230 crore spent in Q1. Management declined to give PCB margin or ROCE targets, saying it was too early and disputing that PCB margins had fallen.

risks_watch: Cash conversion: operating cash flow was negative INR259 crore (another bridge cited INR235 crore), with inventory up INR177 crore; watch whether metering receivables of INR1,311 crore convert and whether the cash-positive target by end FY27 is met.

Margin pressure: component prices up 30-35%, PCB prices up about 3x, lead times 6-8 months, and pass-through to customers lags by a quarter; management said FY27 is a tough year and profitability may take a couple of quarters to normalise.
OSAT and PCB commissioning: Unit 2 and Circuit Chennai guided for Q3 FY27 after West Asia-related slippage; FY27 revenue target INR450-500 crore for both depends on this timeline.
Metering strategy: management is exploring models to divest the service portion to keep receivables off balance sheet, with details promised by February; no concrete plan yet.
Debt and tax clarity: total debt was given as approximately INR800 crore, to be confirmed; consolidated effective tax rate about 35% versus about 23% standalone.
key_quotes: We expect this could take a couple of quarters for profitability to normalize and return to the levels as we had earlier committed to.
Yes, its a difficult year. This year is a difficult year, but I don't think for us whatever we have planned, we will try and meet the requirement. But it is not going to be an easy year.
we are pretty confident that we will be able to do the turnaround by end of this year in terms of receivables from the metering business.
So we don't want to give an absolute number because there is so much of volatility in the market.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on EMS growth and cash turnaround commitments but cautious on FY27 margins, calling it a difficult, tough year. It was evasive on PCB margin and ROCE targets, on metering divestment structure and on exact debt figures, deferring these to later updates.

growth.why: Management committed to 2x market growth with no absolute number, plus a new OSAT+PCB FY27 revenue target of INR450-500 crore backed by Unit 2 and Chennai PCB plant going live by Q3 FY27 and an order book above INR8,900 crore, though margins are pressured and profitability normalisation is pushed out a couple of quarters.
